result.summary: Fixes result code parsing in `PCPRequestPortMap` when checking for NAT-PMP unsupported-version responses during gateway protocol fallback. The code now reads a 16-bit big-endian value at `NATPMP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS` rather than a single byte at `PCP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS`, and switches the version offset constant to `NATPMP_HDR_VERSION_OFS`. A unit test covering 16-bit result codes is added to `pcp_tests.cpp`.
result.problem: When a gateway responds to a Port Control Protocol (PCP) request with an error, `PCPRequestPortMap` checks whether the response is actually an unsupported-version error from a legacy NAT-PMP gateway. The parser incorrectly checked a single byte at offset 3 instead of reading a 16-bit big-endian field starting at offset 2, causing any 16-bit error code ending in byte 1 (e.g., 0x0101) to be falsely recognized as `NATPMP_RESULT_UNSUPP_VERSION`.
evidence: RFC 6886 section 3.5 specifies that NAT-PMP response result codes are 16-bit values.
Lines 348 and 390 in `src/common/pcp.cpp` already read NAT-PMP result codes using `ReadBE16(response.data() + NATPMP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS)`.
result.card: Corrects NAT-PMP fallback error parsing in Port Control Protocol (PCP) port forwarding. PCPRequestPortMap previously read only a single byte at offset 3 instead of a 16-bit big-endian result code at offset 2, causing unrelated error codes ending in byte 1 (like 0x0101) to be misclassified as unsupported-version responses. The fix aligns this check with RFC 6886 and existing NAT-PMP parsing in pcp.cpp, and includes a unit test in pcp_tests.cpp.

risk.why: A flaw in NAT-PMP fallback parsing could cause PCP port-forwarding requests to fail or misidentify router error responses, preventing automatic inbound port mapping.
